title: Case template
tagline: Name the inputs a chain of features is built on -- selections and values -- for case 1, and list the further cases a Case pattern will re-run the chain for.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: To build the same detail on several places (a boss on each of three blocks, each its own height), build it once against names -- #top, #rim, #bossH -- and let a Case pattern re-run it. The Case template defines those names for case 1 and holds the other cases' selections and values.
useWhen: The same feature chain applies to several places
Each place has its own selections and values
A transform pattern cannot do it (the places differ)
slides.caption: The template's case table and the chain built on case A.

slides.title: The dialog
params: The template's own case (default A); its suffix is swapped for each case's name.
Up to 8: a query-variable name and case 1's selection.
Up to 4: a name, a type (Length / Angle / Area / Volume / Number / Text), case 1's value.
Read-only: the inputs as the case rows show them.
One row per case: its name, a selection per input, a value per value.

keys: Query variables bound to case 1's selections.
What the Case pattern reads: every case's selections and values.
messages: Name #x is used twice / Case name "B" is used twice

items.head: Build the chain on the names
items.body: Every listed feature should use #top, #bossH ... -- never a clicked case-1 entity.

items.head: Rows follow the template
items.body: After adding an input or changing a type, edit the template once so every row gets the slot.
